key_concepts: Gravity is a non-contact force that pulls objects toward Earth's surface
Earth's gravity keeps the Moon in orbit as its natural satellite
The Moon has no light of its own and reflects sunlight
The Moon's revolution around Earth causes the observed phases of the Moon
Earth's rotation causes one side to face the Sun as day and the other side as night
Tides are the rise and fall of the ocean surface about every twelve and a half hours
High tide is the highest water level on the seashore and low tide is the lowest
The gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun on Earth's water causes tides
Spring tides are the highest and lowest tides of the month
Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles and produce weaker tides
The predictable interactions of the Sun-Earth-Moon system result in tidal effects
